PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted date]
MEDICAL RECORD: [redacted ID]
REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF COLLECTION: [redacted date]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Amniocentesis performed at 15 weeks gestation by ultrasound dating for prenatal screening of common trisomies.

SPECIMEN
Amniotic fluid (20 mL)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. DNA was extracted from uncultured amniotic fluid cells and amplified using multiplex PCR. Fragment analysis was performed on an Applied Biosystems 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13:
- D13S631: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D13S258: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D13S742: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D13S628: Uninformative (homozygous)
Conclusion: Normal complement for chromosome 13

Chromosome 18:
- D18S391: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D18S390: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D18S535: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D18S386: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
Conclusion: Normal complement for chromosome 18

Chromosome 21:
- D21S1411: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D21S1412: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
- D21S1435: Uninformative (homozygous)
- D21S1446: 1:1 ratio (normal diallelic pattern)
Conclusion: Normal complement for chromosome 21

Sex Chromosome Markers:
- AMELX/Y: XX pattern detected
- SRY: Not detected
Conclusion: Female fetus

INTERPRETATION
No abnormality detected. The QF-PCR analysis shows a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. This result excludes trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in this fetus.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It does not detect structural chromosome abnormalities, mosaicism below 20%, or aneuploidies of other chromosomes. This test does not replace comprehensive chromosome analysis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these normal QF-PCR results, no further chromosome analysis (karyotyping) is required on this sample. Standard prenatal care should continue as clinically indicated.

This test was developed and validated by the [redacted location] Prenatal Genetics Laboratory.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
[redacted date]
